runners_data.name: Tap Dancer

runners_data.name: Rumbustious

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura

runners_data.name: Shifter
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Wilf Storey running off just one day's rest, which is an extreme short turnaround and the trainer's 14-day record of 0/2 is minimal; has placed on good and soft ground at 10f and the 3lb claim from Paula Muir helps, but a true hold-up horse racing in a compressed field on quick rest makes this a speculative each-way proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Parole Officer
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans's 3-year-old steps up markedly in trip from 7-8f to 1m2f — all five career runs have been at 7-8f and there is no evidence of staying this distance; the 52-day absence and headgear (previously hood) add further uncertainty, and as a natural hold-up type displaced from the rear in this field, the combination of trip query and tactical compromise makes this a significant risk.

races.paceDynamic: Sweet Kiss is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will stride into an uncontested position and set a sustainable, honest gallop over Ayr's flat mile-and-two. The pace will not be falsely slow — Sweet Kiss has the ability to control tempo — but without a rival forcing her hand the fractions should be measured and the race effectively run as a test of finishing quality rather than raw stamina. The field is saturated with hold-up types: Condotti, Tee Aitch Aye, Royal Blaze, Tap Dancer, Storm On Jura, Shifter and Parole Officer are all genuine off-the-pace horses redistributed to midfield on the map because they simply cannot all settle as far back as their natural style demands. This tactical verdict is clear: a single uncontested pace-setter on good ground over a flat 1m2f creates a moderately-run race that compresses the field and favours horses who can travel prominently or make sustained ground from midfield — pure sit-and-sprint hold-up horses face the biggest challenge because the pace may not be strong enough to bring them into the race late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sweet Kiss controls, closers chase
scenarios.trigger: If Sweet Kiss dictates an uncontested, moderate tempo and the field fans wide in the straight chasing her.
scenarios.body: Sweet Kiss sets every fraction and the race turns into a prolonged gallop that rewards horses who have tracked her through the middle stages and can sustain their effort; horses who sit just off the pace in the prominent-to-midfield bracket get the ideal tow into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong gallop, late surge wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sweet Kiss is pushed along faster than expected or the pace compresses and horses are forced wider, burning energy earlier.
scenarios.body: A stronger tempo stretches the field sooner, tapping into stamina reserves and allowing horses who have settled deepest to generate late momentum from the back of midfield; the longer 1m2f on good ground over Ayr's flat circuit can reward one powerful late run if the pace is genuinely honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent racer quickens clear
scenarios.trigger: If Sweet Kiss softens the pace enough that a horse tracking her at the head of the main bunch kicks early and goes clear before the hold-up horses can respond.
scenarios.body: A slow-burning race puts a premium on the horse who makes the decisive move first rather than the horse with the most raw finishing kick; any runner able to travel in second or third and strike two furlongs out benefits most from this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, hold-up horse pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Sweet Kiss fades abruptly from the front and creates a genuine late opportunity, allowing horses from well back to close the gap rapidly.
scenarios.body: This shape depends on horses who are true hold-up types finding racing room in the straight and producing a finishing burst, but most of the field's genuine hold-up horses are racing out of their natural role and may be too close to the pace to generate the speed required; the scenario is the least likely given the redistribution and the flat, galloping nature of the Ayr circuit.

watchPoints.text: Sweet Kiss (front-runner) sets the entire tempo — if she is tracked too closely or quickens her fractions in the straight, she becomes a genuine winning threat rather than a pace-setter, and the whole race shape changes if she is allowed to steal first run.

Rumbustious (Connor Beasley, OR 65) is the top-rated runner and has consistent placed form at this trip and going — watch for Beasley positioning him prominently off the pace and using the flat Ayr straight to challenge; he is the horse most likely to improve beyond his mapping position.

Naturalia's record of five places at similar going (1W 5P from 7 runs) flags her as a consistent hanger-on who keeps finding the frame; Shay Farmer's 5lb claim could be decisive in a compressed finish and she should not be underestimated if she gets a clear run.

Parole Officer has never run beyond 8f and steps to 1m2f here — the trip doubt is significant and worth monitoring in-running to see whether she weakens sharply once the race enters its final quarter-mile, which would indicate the distance is beyond her current range.

Storm On Jura's fade flag combined with a 6-day turnaround means she is a horse to track early in the race — if she is prominent early and tiring before the home turn, it confirms the pace has been genuine enough to suit the closers, providing a useful in-running read on the shape of the finish.

runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo has placed form on Good ground but is a genuine hold-up performer who will likely race further back than the map position suggests, making its task entirely dependent on pace developing sufficiently; six runs at this trip and going show only one win and one place from six.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: Stepping up to 7f for the first time after a run of 5f-6f form, and while there is placed form on Good ground, the trip is an unknown; a true rear-of-field operator who will be further back than shown, and the 14-of-6f-soft last time is a concern on today's ground.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 4yo boasts a win and two places in the last five runs and has recent Good-ground form at 7f that reads well for today, but as a genuine hold-up performer placed into midfield on the map, Lauren Young (5) will need things to fall kindly to produce the finish from further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Blakefell
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; Ivan Furtado's 3yo won over this exact course and distance on Good ground and has strong 7f form, and Tom Eaves will be able to set the fractions entirely on his own terms — the Style_Fit tag reflects that he is mapped slightly out of role here, but his lead position is confirmed and his recent form is strong.

runners_data.name: Qazaq
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago for Iain Jardine, who is in excellent recent form (9/31 over 14 days), but the quick turnaround for a 5yo hold-up type who has not won in 15 comparable starts is a significant flag; will settle at the back and relies on a strong gallop to make up ground.

runners_data.name: Slack Bob
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's 3yo carries natural hold-up tendencies but has shown a placed effort on Good ground at 8f and a win at 7f on Standard; the drop back in company relative to some recent runs gives a small angle, though Clifford Lee will need a well-run race to produce his finish.

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 8yo holds the highest racecard weight (142lbs) and has placed twice on Good ground at 7f, but has not hit the frame in his last four runs at the trip; ran six days ago, which combined with the age and weight makes this a tough ask, even with Goldie's yard in form.

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 7yo has won three of his last five starts including back-to-back wins on Good and Soft at 7f, and Andrew Mullen consistently delivers for the yard; a natural prominent runner, he is ideally placed to track Blakefell and quicken late, making him one of the most profile-fitting runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 4yo won over this course and trip on Good ground earlier in the season but has since posted 11th, 15th, and 10th in three subsequent runs on comparable ground; a hold-up type whose inconsistency is stark, and Paul Mulrennan will need significant improvement on recent outings.

runners_data.name: Eve's Boy
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' 4yo has finished second and sixth in the last two starts and has placed form at 8f on Good ground, though today's 7f trip looks a touch sharp based on hist; last ran 40 days ago, the longest absence in the field, and has not won in fifteen tries on comparable going.

races.paceDynamic: Blakefell is the confirmed lone front-runner here, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Tom Eaves can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 7f on Good ground — the absence of pressure means fractions will be honest rather than fierce, and the pace will not collapse. Keep Me Stable and The Gay Blade are the two natural prominent-racers who will look to sit just off Blakefell's shoulder and cover their positions early, giving them a potent stalking role through the middle stages. Behind them, the midfield and hold-up section is unusually congested: Born A Star, Ashen, Whiskey Kisses, Qazaq, and Emery Down are all genuine rear-of-field types who have been pushed forward on the map because the race cannot physically accommodate that many closers at the back — in reality several will race further back than shown and face a stiffer task. With a single front-runner setting a fair but uncontested tempo on a flat track, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader without burning their engine and pounce in the final two furlongs, making a tracking position from Keep Me Stable or The Gay Blade the tactically optimal profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blakefell Leads, Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Blakefell dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and prominent chasers track efficiently through the bend.
scenarios.body: Blakefell sets a controlled pace that keeps the race together until the two-furlong pole, at which point The Gay Blade and Keep Me Stable, travelling within themselves just off the lead, have the energy reserves to accelerate and overhaul him; the even tempo suits horses who can quicken from a handy position on this flat track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Defies Field
scenarios.trigger: If Blakefell is allowed such a soft lead that he builds an unassailable advantage and the hold-up runners cannot bridge the gap.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to apply early pressure, Eaves engineers a comfortable rhythm and Blakefell simply never gets headed, the finishing kick of the closers blunted by an insufficient pace to bring them into play in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Get Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sharper than expected and Blakefell's early dominance causes the field to fan wide, opening a lane for genuine closers.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger gallop burns off the prominent pair and creates a true test, bringing Ashen and Abduction — both effective on this Good ground at 7f — into contention from off the pace, though their redistributed map positions mean they face a wider draw of luck.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Blakefell goes too slowly and the field concertinas into a bunched sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A muddling tempo leaves the entire field in contention turning for home and produces a wall-to-wall sprint that randomises the result, slightly favouring horses with raw finishing speed and lower weight; Slack Bob's recent placed form at this distance becomes relevant.

watchPoints.text: Blakefell (Tom Eaves) is the sole front-runner in a 12-runner field — if he bowls along unchallenged and sets a comfortable rhythm, he becomes genuinely hard to peg back and could convert his lead position into a front-running victory rather than simply setting the pace for others.

The Gay Blade has won three of five recent starts on Good ground at 7f and will aim to sit directly behind Blakefell; if he gets a clean run into the straight from a prominent position, his sharp finishing speed over this trip makes him the most dangerous stalker in the race.

Iain Jardine runs both The Gay Blade and Qazaq in this race — watch for any jockey instructions that suggest one is ridden as a pacemaker or to assist the other, as a stable with 9 winners from 31 runners in 14 days could be working a plan.

Several hold-up types (Born A Star, Ashen, Whiskey Kisses, Emery Down, Qazaq) will all be competing for the same limited late ground in the straight — if they fan wide on the home turn looking for room, traffic interference is a live risk and may cost one or more a clear run.

Keep Me Stable is 14 days fresh and Kaiya Fraser's trainer Linda Perratt is 0/4 in the last fortnight — monitor market confidence in the morning, as any significant drift could signal that the recent losing run from the yard is a genuine concern rather than coincidence.

races.paceDynamic: Penelope's Sister is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no meaningful challenger for the early lead, she should dictate from the front at a sustainable, even gallop over this flat Ayr mile on Good turf. Hey Havana and Concert Boy will look to press into prominent positions just behind her, meaning the head of affairs is unlikely to be seriously contested but the pace should be honest rather than pedestrian. The hold-up contingent — Hunterian, Starliner, Ey Up He's A Star, and technically Flying Moonlight, Lightning Galaxy and Lovette — will be funnelled into midfield and the rear, but the field contains more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the back, with Lovette, Lightning Galaxy and Flying Moonlight all redistribued toward the middle of the pack despite preferring a closer position to the tail of the field. With a lone front-runner setting a controlled pace, the race strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or in the first half of the field and quicken from a close-up position, rather than those waiting on a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Penelope's Sister Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Penelope's Sister secures an uncontested lead and sets a steady, sustainable pace that her rivals cannot wind back.
scenarios.body: She dictates every fraction without pressure, ensuring the race is run to suit those travelling close to her, and horses who track her in the first two or three off the pace have an energy advantage when the tempo lifts in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Quicken Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Hey Havana and Concert Boy push Penelope's Sister into a stronger gallop and the race develops into a sustained two-furlong battle from the front.
scenarios.body: A more pressured pace brings the prominent group into play and tests Penelope's Sister's ability to sustain her effort, opening the door for a prominent hold-up horse who tracks the pace closely to sprint clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and the field bunches, allowing genuine hold-up types to produce late runs.
scenarios.body: Starliner and Hunterian, both carrying form on this course and distance, have the profile to arrive late if gaps open, though this scenario is discounted because most natural hold-up runners are redistributed into mid-pack rather than racing from their preferred rear position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If early traffic issues or a wide-margin collapse in the midfield group produces an unusually messy race with position changes throughout.
scenarios.body: Redistributed horses like Lovette and Lightning Galaxy, forced to race closer than ideal, could either benefit if the pace is strong and they gain cover, or suffer if they lose momentum in traffic, making the result highly unpredictable.

watchPoints.text: Penelope's Sister sets the entire pace narrative — if she is allowed a soft, unchallenged lead by Hey Havana and Concert Boy, front-rank horses dominate; watch whether she is immediately pressed out of the stalls.

Hey Havana is one of two prominent types who could actively disrupt Penelope's Sister's control; if Clifford Lee sends him forward early to test the pace, the whole dynamic shifts toward a more gruelling finish that suits hold-up types.

Starliner carries top weight (142lbs) and has a habit of finishing strongly on Good ground at Ayr; watch whether Kaiya Fraser can find a clean run from mid-division, as late-closing scenarios hinge on his ability to get daylight in the final furlong.

Lovette, Lightning Galaxy and Flying Moonlight are all natural hold-up horses racing closer than ideal due to redistribution — if any of these three finds itself trapped wide or behind a wall of rivals in the straight, their chance is effectively gone regardless of pace.

Concert Boy has a poor record on Good turf (1 from 15) but Greg Fairley may use him as a pace-presence rather than a winner, which could inadvertently help shape the race for Hey Havana tracking directly behind.

races.paceDynamic: Territorial Knight is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 6f handicap and, with no serious challenger willing to take him on from the gate, he should slot into an uncontested lead at a sustainable but honest Good-ground gallop. Parisiac, Rousing Encore and Cotai Lights will push up prominently behind him, creating a compact early order at the head of affairs, but the pace is unlikely to be truly strong — one horse dictating from the front rarely generates the searching fractions that blow the field apart. The large field holds substantially more hold-up types than can realistically find their natural position: Manila Scouse, Here Forever, Prince Of Pillo, Dakota Gold and others have been remapped to midfield, but in an 18-runner sprint the genuine closers will be buried wide or deep and will need a generous split of fortune to land a telling blow. On this race shape — a controlled solo lead, honest but not blistering fractions on Good ground — prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and quicken in the final furlong hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Territorial Knight Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Territorial Knight secures the lead unchallenged and dictates a comfortable tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: He bowls along on the far rail, sets an honest but unhurried pace, and the field strings out behind him; those sitting second or third have first run and can outstay him inside the final furlong. Prominent types like Parisiac and Cotai Lights, travelling sweetly just off the leader, are best placed to collar him late or run him down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely steady and the race resolves into a sprint finish between those who raced in the first five.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run 6f on Good ground compresses the field and turns the closing stages into a furlong-long dash where position is everything; horses who were handy throughout have no traffic issues and produce maximum finishing energy. Parisiac, who has won and placed repeatedly in recent form, and Cotai Lights, capable of finishing fast from a prominent pitch, are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front end burns brighter than expected and the pace collapses in the final furlong, opening a gap for the deeper held-up horses.
scenarios.body: Woven and Manila Scouse, genuine hold-up types who sit last or near-last, would need the pace to blow up entirely and a clear wide passage through a packed 18-runner field — a low-probability combination on a flat 6f track with a controlled lead. Even if the front falters, most redistributed hold-up horses are mapped to midfield and are unlikely to be in the true back-group required to benefit fully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Shock
scenarios.trigger: If interference or a fractious start causes a bunched, chaotic break and the race unfolds without a settled front-runner.
scenarios.body: Tactical chaos in a large 18-runner field can produce a falsely-run race that rewards whoever gets a clear, uncrowded passage; lightly-raced Tip Foster, with just two runs, is unpredictable enough in this scenario, while Daizen has won twice and handles Good ground well. These horses carry low weights and are unrestricted by a specific positional requirement that the chaos has voided.

watchPoints.text: Parisiac (OR=80) has won and placed at 5–6f in five of his last five starts with Jardine's yard firing (7 wins/14 days) — if he gets a clean pitch in third or fourth and the pace is honest, he is the most dangerous horse in the race from a positional standpoint.

The field contains at least eight genuine hold-up types compressed into a midfield map; if they all attempt to come wide and late simultaneously in the closing furlong of a 6f sprint, significant interference and checked runs are likely — horses drawn low and wide may be hardest hit.

Territorial Knight has been off 65 days and faces a true front-running assignment rather than his natural prominent role; if he ties up under pressure inside the final furlong having led alone, the horses immediately behind him will be the prime beneficiaries.

Tip Foster is only two runs into her career and her Going profile on Good ground is entirely untested — if she handles the surface and settles, the low weight and yard form (David & Nicola Barron placed Here Forever recently) make her a chaos wildcard worth monitoring in running.

Cotai Lights has been off 50 days but showed consistent placed form earlier in the season; watch whether Mikey Sheehy presses up to sit second or third on the rail, as that position in a controlled-pace race could prove crucial in the final 2f.

races.name: 25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, giving him a structural edge at this trip; goes on good ground (1 win from 1 on similar), but the STYLE_FIT tag notes he is technically prominent rather than a pure leader, and Linda Perratt's yard is winless in the last 14 days from 8 runners — conditions suit but support angles are modest.

runners_data.name: Joshuas Dream
runners_data.note: A 247-day absence makes this a significant fitness query for a two-year-old stepping up to 6f; has placed form on good ground from five runs but the layoff and youth make him a considerable unknown, and his hold-up style leaves him dependent on a truly-run race that may not materialise.

runners_data.name: Keep The Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a solid placing record on good ground (2 wins from 5 placed at similar conditions), wearing a hood today; steps up from his usual 5f and that extra furlong may help him sustain his finish, but he needs the pace to be honest to do his best work from off it.

runners_data.name: April Diamond
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse reassigned to midfield on the map because genuine closers are overcrowded at the rear in this field — the 0.90 style-fit flag tempers confidence she will operate in her preferred way; her best recent form is a second on good over 6f, and Iain Jardine has been active with runners but with modest recent returns.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: Five from eight in the places on good ground is a strong credentials marker, and Sean Bowen takes over in the saddle which is a notable jockey upgrade; naturally races held up but has placed off moderate pace before, and the 26-day freshener may suit a three-year-old still developing.

runners_data.name: Maynora
runners_data.note: Wore a hood today and gets a slight trip relief stepping back to 6f; the trainer is winless in 16 days and Maynora's recent form shows a string of mid-division finishes with one win on soft — the good ground here is less proven territory, and her hold-up style leaves her exposed in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: Has two wins and four places from 15 career runs, all over 5f, making this 6f trip an untested stretch; a true closer pushed forward on the map by field composition, the STYLE_FIT tag is warranted — he has not won on good going in 12 attempts at similar conditions, which compounds the positional and trip concern.

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose recent form reads 9th, 10th and 13th in three of the last four starts, all on going ranging from good to soft; Easterby yard has been busy but the horse's current form trajectory is hard to get enthusiastic about, and being a hold-up type in a slowly-run 6f field compounds the challenge.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly wearing a hood, trained by Daragh Bourke who has had limited runners; her best finish of 4th has come twice on good ground over 6f, which provides some relevance, but her natural hold-up style has been displaced to midfield and the 0.90 style-fit means she is unlikely to race where she is shown.

runners_data.name: Ellie's de Vega
runners_data.note: Remarkable consistency — five runs, three thirds on good ground over 6f — and she is one of only three natural prominent horses in the race, meaning she will get her position behind the leader naturally; the headgear flag (hood) continues from last time and Ryan Sexton has been associated with her progressive profile.

runners_data.name: Newyorkstateofmind
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran wearing a blinker, whose redistribution to midfield masks his true hold-up preference in a field already crowded with closers; modest recent form (8th, 6th, 4th) on good ground suggests he is running below his OR peak, and the style mismatch in a slowly-run race is a serious structural obstacle.

runners_data.name: Baby Rover
runners_data.note: One of only three prominent-style horses in the race, which immediately gives her a positional advantage in what figures to be a moderately-paced affair; her best recent run was a 2nd over 6f on good ground, and Katie Scott's yard has had a recent winner in the last 14 days — she maps well to this race shape.

runners_data.name: Saxon Gem
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's yard has been firing — 6 from 37 in 14 days — but Saxon Gem herself has posted five consecutive finishes of 4th to 7th, all on good ground over 6f-8f; a true hold-up type shuffled to midfield by field dynamics, her consistency in defeat rather than victory is the recurring theme and the race shape does her no favours.

races.paceDynamic: Henery Hawk is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 6f handicap on good ground at Ayr, and with Ellie's de Vega and Baby Rover as the only other prominent-style horses, the pace is unlikely to be contested aggressively — Henery Hawk should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo without being seriously pressured. That moderate, uncontested lead over 6f on good ground creates a race that plays squarely into the hands of prominent racers who can track the pace and produce a finish, rather than those needing a strong gallop to close into. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — April Diamond, Saxon Grace, Royal Duke, So Grateful, Saxon Gem, Newyorkstateofmind and others are genuine closers who have been redistributed forward on the map simply because there is insufficient natural cover at the rear; several of these will be unable to get their preferred position in what is a moderate-tempo race. The clear tactical verdict is that prominent and pace-tracking profiles are favoured: a controlled lead from Henery Hawk, tracked by Ellie's de Vega and Baby Rover, sets up a race where those who can press or sit just off the pace into the home straight hold a structural advantage over the hold-up brigade who will have ground to make up with little strong pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Henery Hawk Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Henery Hawk is allowed to stride clear from the front and the field fails to close the gap approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Henery Hawk sets a comfortable pace without pressure, conserves energy through the middle portion, and the lack of a strong sustained gallop means closers find it hard to reel him in over a short 6f trip; his good-ground form (1 win at similar conditions) underpins the threat.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Ellie's de Vega or Baby Rover track Henery Hawk closely and produce a stronger late kick to nail him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With only moderate pace set, the horses positioned just off the lead travelling comfortably into the home turn are ideally placed to pick up and go past a tiring leader; Ellie's de Vega's consistent placed record at this course and distance (five runs, three thirds on good) makes her the chief beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Manage To Close
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected or the hold-up horses are ridden more aggressively to secure a better position, allowing them to launch a meaningful late challenge.
scenarios.body: White Ladder and Keep The Gold, who have placed form on good ground over similar trips, represent the best-credentialled of the deeper-drawn closers and would benefit most if the pace quickens mid-race and creates a genuine target to close into; however, the structural reality of a lightly-pressured field means this is the least straightforward path to victory for these types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Hold-Up Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the final furlong and a well-handicapped, fresh-legged hold-up horse finishes through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape dependent on redistribution horses — Royal Duke, Saxon Grace or Newyorkstateofmind — racing genuinely held up and picking up late, which runs against the grain of a moderate-tempo 6f where gaps close quickly; the style-fit penalties and poor recent form of several in this group further reduce the chance of this shape producing a winner.

watchPoints.text: Henery Hawk's ability to dictate an uncontested, comfortable pace is the single biggest race-shaping factor — watch whether Ellie's de Vega or Baby Rover apply any early pressure, as even moderate competition could drain his reserves by the final furlong.

Ellie's de Vega's five-run placed consistency at exactly this trip and going combination makes her the most dangerous horse to track in the market — if she travels smoothly in second and picks up well inside the final furlong, she has the profile to collect.

The cluster of hold-up horses — April Diamond, Saxon Grace, Royal Duke and Saxon Gem — are all flagged as redistributed and carry style-fit discounts; watch the market to see if any of these are heavily backed, which would represent a positional assumption that the race shape may not support.

Baby Rover's jockey Joanna Mason is known for front-running tactics and could attempt to push for a lead role alongside Henery Hawk — if she does, the pace dynamic becomes contested and the race shape shifts meaningfully toward a stronger-run affair that opens the door for hold-up horses.

White Ladder's jockey booking of Sean Bowen represents the most significant rider upgrade in the field — monitor his pre-race market move closely, as sharp support for a horse that has solid placed form on good ground would signal professional intent in what could be an open finish.

races.name: Dream Weddings At Western House Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse from Iain Jardine's yard; best form at 12-16f on standard and good ground, but six recent runs at this trip level show only one placing without a win — needs traffic to clear.|

runners_data.name: Idyllic
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday (1 day since last run), which is a significant fitness and fatigue flag; Paula Muir claims 3lb but the horse's form shows consistent out-of-the-frame finishes, and no win at this distance suggests a difficult task.|

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran for Jim Goldie who is a genuine hold-up performer in reality, though placed into a midfield map slot here due to field composition; arrives off an 11-day break with two recent wins at 11-14f on good ground and is arguably the most in-form horse in the race.|

runners_data.name: Is She Now
runners_data.note: Won twice in five runs (most recently at 12-13f on good and soft) and is genuinely a closer by nature, shown in midfield here only because the rear is oversubscribed — David Nolan takes the ride and the horse returns on a short six-day turnaround for a trainer with just 1 win from 2 recent runs.|

runners_data.name: Galahad Threepwood
runners_data.note: Oldest runner at nine years and a true hold-up type bumped forward on the map by traffic; best form is at very long trips (17-21f) so this 1m5f may be on the sharp side, and Greg Fairley partners a horse who hasn't won in recent form (9435/7).|

runners_data.name: Aighear
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's second runner; a confirmed closer whose recent form (123-34) is honest rather than spectacular, placed third at 15-16f on good and soft — the STYLE_FIT tag notes she's racing out of natural position on the map, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim helps the weight.|

runners_data.name: Ebony Maw
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' nine-year-old wearing tongue-tie and blinkers — genuine hold-up type that the map has shifted forward; best runs have come at 15-16f on soft, so this good ground at 1m5f is at the outer edge of his comfort zone after 17 days off.|

runners_data.name: La Tosca
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Charlie Johnston's powerful yard carrying 121lbs and ridden by Sean Bowen; the form string (434222) is a model of consistent placing without winning, and the historical profile shows she handles good ground at 12-15f well — likely to sit close to the pace and stay on honestly.|

runners_data.name: This Rib
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the race, but flagged with STYLE_FIT concerns; her entire form history is at 7-8f, making this 1m5f a massive step up in trip, and recent form (846-P0) is deeply uninspiring — Joanna Mason takes over but the question is whether she can truly see out the distance after setting the pace.|

races.paceDynamic: This Rib is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of nine over 1m5f on good ground at Ayr, and with no genuine rival willing to press from the outset, she should be able to dictate a controlled, measured tempo from the front. The danger is not a pace battle but rather a well-judged lead that suits a horse who can conserve energy and quicken off a sustainable gallop — though her recent form (846-P0) and step up in trip from sprint distances raise serious doubts about whether she can actually exploit that position. The rest of the field — Annandale, Is She Now, Galahad Threepwood, Aighear, and Ebony Maw — are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots on the map simply because there are more closers than the rear positions can accommodate; none of them are front-runners by trade. This field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can place at the back, with Annandale and Is She Now — both recent winners and the most in-form of the group — most likely to secure the best tracking positions just off the pace. The dominant scenario is a steady-to-fair pace set by This Rib that rewards horses who can travel powerfully through the race and quicken late, giving a material edge to the strongest closers who can find clear daylight in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If This Rib sets an unhurried pace and the field strings out behind her, allowing the strongest finishers to pick her off approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This Rib controls from the front without being seriously challenged, but the sustainable gallop over 1m5f on good ground sets up perfectly for hold-up runners with a strong late kick to reel her in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If This Rib jumps well, establishes a clear lead early, and the hold-up pack get bunched, failing to deliver a co-ordinated challenge in time.
scenarios.body: With the closers impeded or slow to organise behind her, This Rib's uncontested lead becomes a winning platform despite her modest form, and the race is over before the field can close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Surge Decides
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or midfield horse like Annandale or La Tosca makes an assertive move from 3f out, driving the tempo up before the field fully awakens.
scenarios.body: An early commitment to close on This Rib splits the field and rewards the horse with the best combination of stamina and resolution at this trip, particularly those proven at 1m3f-1m5f on good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Chaos, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely or This Rib is taken wide early and the field idles, allowing a well-handicapped outsider to nick the race in a messy finish.
scenarios.body: A lack of any meaningful gallop turns the race into a sprint home from two furlongs out, exposing horses who have been slowly drawn into the race, and a course-fit or fresh handler-in-form runner benefits.

watchPoints.text: This Rib's stamina is completely unproven beyond 8f — watch for her to dramatically shorten stride or capitulate turning for home, which would fundamentally change how the finish unfolds and who benefits.

Annandale is the standout form horse in the field with two recent wins at this trip on good ground, but is a true hold-up runner shown in midfield — watch for Paul Mulrennan to angle wide early to secure a clear tracking position rather than get buried in a crowd.

La Tosca has six consecutive placed efforts without a win and could easily post another honest second or third — watch for her to travel well and look a danger entering the straight before being outstayed or outpointed close home.

Idyllic ran just yesterday — monitor for any withdrawal or signs of distress in the paddock; if she runs, her freshness and jumping ability from the gate will be severely compromised and she is a risk to race erratically.

With five genuine hold-up horses funnelled into a midfield map and only one front-runner, the key tactical moment will come 3-4f out — watch which horse first commits to closing on This Rib, as that move is likely to define the winner.
